<a id="continuation-relative-to-a-class--相对于类的续"></a>
# Continuation relative to a class

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`continuation-relative-to-a-class` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](continuation-relative-to-a-class.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> For every carrier and relation, continuation is 缘 met with a class; its positions depend on the class, a class constant under 缘 never lets a continuation end, a line's own regularity is the class's core, and the old base's arising, ceasing, lineage and passing are its instances.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. Continuation is 缘 met with a class: one occurrence continues another under a class where the first is a condition of the second and the two are alike under the class. A line is the reach of continuation, and an occurrence begins, abides or ends in it where it has no predecessor, both, or no successor; beginning and abiding exclude each other, as do abiding and ending, and every line runs along the reach of 缘. (`Becoming.«续»`, `Becoming.«相续»`, `Becoming.«有前»`, `Becoming.«有后»`, `Becoming.«生»`, `Becoming.«住»`, `Becoming.«亡»`, `Becoming.«异»`, `Becoming.«续含于缘»`, `Becoming.«相续含于及»`, `Becoming.«生住不并»`, `Becoming.«住亡不并»`)
2. No position stands by itself: the positions depend on the class. Under the one, continuation is 缘 itself, and an occurrence begins exactly where nothing conditions it; in a net without self-conditioning, an occurrence with a condition and a consequence abides under the one and both begins and ends under identity. (`Becoming.«一之续»`, `Becoming.«一之生»`, `Becoming.«四相无自立»`)
3. Coarsening: under a coarser class every continuation remains one, so what ends under the coarser class ends under the finer and what abides under the finer abides under the coarser; something can end under the finer class while it abides under the coarser. (`Becoming.«粗化»`, `Becoming.«亡于粗则亡于细»`, `Becoming.«住于细则住于粗»`, `Becoming.«亡于细者不必亡于粗»`)
4. A class constant under 缘 (E˘;R ⊆ R;E˘) never lets a continuation end: whatever continues something is continued, symmetric class or not. So a class under which some line ends is not constant, and a line that ends has its own regularity in its class's core, not in the class. (`Becoming.«有常»`, `Becoming.«有常之逐点»`, `Becoming.«有常则续不尽»`, `Becoming.«有常则相续不尽»`, `Becoming.«有亡之续则不有常»`)
5. The core of a class under 缘 lies inside it, is constant and symmetric, and contains every symmetric constant relation inside it: it is the greatest one, and the core of a class is a class. Read both ways, constant under 缘 and under its converse, the core fixes positions: what shares it shares beginning and ending. (`Becoming.«核»`, `Becoming.«根»`, `Becoming.«核为类»`, `Becoming.«有常可复合»`, `Becoming.«静有常»`, `Becoming.«位核»`, `Becoming.«位根»`, `Becoming.«位核含于核»`, `Becoming.«亡于核下不变»`, `Becoming.«生于位核下不变»`, `Becoming.«位同则四相同»`)
6. Continuation is not defined through the core: in a flame of three moments ending in ash, the moments continue one another under 'flame or not', yet under that class's core no two occurrences continue one another, since the moments' futures differ by how long is left. (`Becoming.Flame`, `Becoming.Flame.step`, `Becoming.Flame.burns`, `Becoming.Flame.alike`, `Becoming.Flame.alike_class`, `Becoming.Flame.not_core_f₁`, `Becoming.Flame.not_core_f₀`, `Becoming.«以核为判据则火无续»`)
7. For a class, constancy is exactly closure of the coarse net: E;R;E ⊆ R;E. Read without taking classes apart, every 缘 inside a class becomes a loop at both its ends; the coarse net therefore takes 缘 between classes, and it joins only different classes. (`Becoming.«闭合当且仅当有常»`, `Becoming.«类内之缘成环»`, `Becoming.«粗»`, `Becoming.«粗只连异类»`)
8. Renewal: an occurrence renews where it is a condition of a beginning that goes on; renewal at the grain of a class reads the same relation at that grain, and every renewal is one at every grain. Renewal without end is the greatest family each member of which renews into a line reaching the family again; it renews. Under the one there is neither. (`Becoming.«复生»`, `Becoming.«粗复生»`, `Becoming.«复生则粗复生»`, `Becoming.«一之下无复生»`, `Becoming.«生生»`, `Becoming.«生生之展»`, `Becoming.«生生最大»`, `Becoming.«生生则复生»`, `Becoming.«一之下无生生»`)
9. Boundaries in the grammar itself: that every occurrence, in every model, either begins or has a predecessor is exactly excluded middle; under fission, sameness read along lines either way is not transitive; every single 缘 is a continuation under some class, and two alike conditions of one occurrence make a merge; reach is an order of precedence only where nothing reaches itself. (`Becoming.«四相之定当且仅当排中»`, `Becoming.«分叉»`, `Becoming.«同族»`, `Becoming.«同族为类»`, `Becoming.«任一缘可为续»`, `Becoming.«蜡烛之合»`, `Becoming.«无环»`, `Becoming.«无环则及为序»`, `Becoming.«不穷»`)
10. Lines: a line under a class stays within it; a beginning under a finer class continued under a coarser one is an alteration; what begins under a coarser class begins under the finer; and where every step keeps a class or carries a mark, a line whose ends the class tells apart has a marked step. (`Becoming.«线内同类»`, `Becoming.«生于细而续于粗则异»`, `Becoming.«生于粗则生于细»`, `Becoming.«两端分则中有标»`)
11. Holding, mutual need and leaning-on through constancy apply only to lines that do not end; through the core they apply to all: a class suffices for another's regularity where what is alike under both is alike under the other's core. The constancy forms imply the core forms, a class is constant exactly where it lies in its core, and a flame's regularity lies in fire and fuel. (`Becoming.«自持»`, `Becoming.«相须»`, `Becoming.«因于»`, `Becoming.«有常之同谓»`, `Becoming.«相须之对称»`, `Becoming.«无自相须»`, `Becoming.«核之单调»`, `Becoming.«类有常当且仅当含于核»`, `Becoming.«足以定理»`, `Becoming.«因于核»`, `Becoming.«相须核»`, `Becoming.«合有常则足以定理»`, `Becoming.«因于则因于核»`, `Becoming.«相须则相须核»`, `Becoming.Flame.fuel`, `Becoming.Flame.sameFuel`, `Becoming.Flame.joint_eq`, `Becoming.«火因于薪»`)
12. Ceasing: nothing on the line from an occurrence renews. Renewal without end does not cease (生生不息), and under the one everything ceases. (`Becoming.«息»`, `Becoming.«生生不息»`, `Becoming.«一之下皆息»`)
13. The old base's arising and ceasing along one relatum are beginning and ending under 'alike in activity', occurrences being pairs of a step and a relatum; ceasing to be is an ending and coming to be a beginning; the finite-world law of arising and ceasing is exactly the decidability of the positions. (`Becoming.Web.arises_iff_sheng`, `Becoming.Web.unceasing_iff_late_beginnings`, `Becoming.Web.renews_iff`, `Becoming.Steps.next`, `Becoming.Steps.along`, `Becoming.Web.activityClass`, `Becoming.ceasesToBe_iff_wang`, `Becoming.comesToBe_iff_sheng`, `Becoming.Web.ceases_iff_wang`, `Becoming.positions_iff_em`, `Becoming.persists_of_positions`, `Becoming.core_iff_same_course`, `Becoming.Web.flash_positions`, `Becoming.World.law_iff_positions`, `Becoming.World.law_iff_grammar_positions`)
14. Relative to a continuation of the old base, arising and ceasing are its beginning and ending; a split is fission and a merge the candles' merge; lineages, continuing, links and holding are lines, unchanged by re-identification. (`Becoming.Web.continuationStep`, `Becoming.Web.arisesFrom_iff_sheng`, `Becoming.Web.ceasesFrom_iff_wang`, `Becoming.Web.split_fission`, `Becoming.Web.merge_candles`, `Becoming.Web.lineage_iff_line`, `Becoming.Web.positions_not_self_standing`, `Becoming.Web.reach_strict_order`, `Becoming.Web.continuing_iff_line`, `Becoming.Web.linked_iff_line`, `Becoming.Web.held_iff_line`, `Becoming.Web.RenewingAlong.branches`, `Becoming.Web.ConsumingAlong.merged_candles`, `Becoming.Web.line_reidentify`)
15. Passing a pattern on while the carrier ceases is an alteration, ending under the carrier class and continuing under the pattern's (火传); falling dormant is an alteration under holding, and choosing what holds is choosing a class. (`Becoming.Web.carrierClass`, `Becoming.Web.byPassing_iff_hasPred`, `Becoming.Web.passing_fire`, `Becoming.PatternRelay.fire_shape`, `Becoming.Web.stateClass`, `Becoming.Web.fallsDormant_alters`, `Becoming.Web.ceases_of_persisting_ceases`, `Becoming.Hibernation.positions`, `Becoming.Seed.held_classes`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- None beyond the grammar: every carrier and every relation; where a theorem speaks of a class, the class is an equivalence relation.
- Equality on the carrier is a commitment of the model, used where identity is a class (the positions under identity, the flame, the merge).

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- That a class is warranted: constancy says only that a class agrees with 缘; under the full relation every class is constant.
- That continuation contained in 缘 tells a fire passed on from one fire ending and another starting: every single 缘 is a continuation under some class, and two alike conditions make a merge. Witness: `Becoming.«任一缘可为续»`.
- That renewal without end tells renewal that sustains life from turnover that destroys it.
- That reach orders occurrences where conditions are mutual: it is then a preorder.
- That the old base's counting, amounts, recurrence and renaming laws are instances: the grammar states no counting and no map of carriers, so only their premises are connected.
- **Counterexample:** A flame of three moments ending in ash continues under 'flame or not' and has no continuation under that class's core («以核为判据则火无续»). [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Grammar.lean)
- **Counterexample:** Fission: one occurrence continued by two that go no further makes sameness along lines intransitive («分叉»). [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Grammar.lean)

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used. · Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · A law of the formal model; its correspondence to actual systems is a separate obligation.

## Next

<details><summary>Correspondence, dependencies, sources and history</summary>

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

For a class, constancy is bisimulation equivalence (Park 1981; Milner 1989) and the core the greatest bisimulation inside the class; reach is the transitive closure of the calculus of relations (Tarski 1941). Continuation relative to a class is close to genidentity (Lewin 1922) and to Whitehead's enduring objects (1929); the closure law is the relational analogue of lumpability (Kemeny and Snell 1960) and of computational closure (Rosas et al. 2024), a correspondence not proved here. The classical readings (四相 in 《大乘起信论》, 六相 in 《金师子章》, 一实 in 《荀子·正名》, the refutation of 相續 in 《中论》) are registered with their losses in the plan.

<a id="dependencies--依赖"></a>
### Dependencies

- none
- related, not a proved adapter: [classes-along-a-continuation](classes-along-a-continuation.md). There formation classes are read along a given continuation of the old base, with splits and merges; here continuation itself is 缘 met with a class, for every carrier and relation.
- related, not a proved adapter: [a-pattern-lasts-through-passing](a-pattern-lasts-through-passing.md). A pattern outlasting its carriers there is a line under a class here; lifting it is the next step.
- related, not a proved adapter: [branching-tests-bisimulation](branching-tests-bisimulation.md). Bisimulation there is between labelled processes; here the core is the greatest symmetric relation constant under one relation inside a class.

<a id="history--沿革"></a>
